answer: Under interference-bounded radio enrollment, each identity is admitted only by transmitting a one-bit reply at a secret nanosecond the registry assigns by hashing its key, so simultaneous fake registrations physically collide and only one succeeds per slot per channel across the karst uplink, the oasis relay, and the mesa backbone. A mass attacker pushing 1,000 fake agents must serialize through about 1,000·log₂(1,000)≈10,000 slot rounds, and each collision forces a full retransmit, so cost grows nonlinearly with batch size.
